title: On-Device Learning, Federated Systems, and Privacy

content.value: Primary reading: Machine Learning Systems, Chapters 14 and 15. Supplemental: federated learning and on-device ML materials.

This unit moves beyond centralized training and serving. Students study on-device inference, on-device adaptation, federated learning, privacy-preserving data flows, secure aggregation, differential privacy ideas, device heterogeneity, intermittent connectivity, and update management. The systems theme is heterogeneity: clients differ in compute, data, energy, network quality, reliability, and local objectives. Privacy is treated as an architecture constraint that affects data movement, observability, debugging, and evaluation.
Supplemental sources for this unit are listed in the references below. Use them to compare the textbook framing with public talks, documentation, papers, and production guidance.
Studio: design a federated learning plan for a mobile keyboard model. Deliverable: client eligibility rules, aggregation plan, privacy controls, monitoring limitations, and failure modes.

concepts.name: On-device inference
concepts.description: Running model predictions directly on a user device or local hardware.

concepts.name: Federated learning
concepts.description: Training models across distributed devices or clients while keeping raw data local.

concepts.name: Local training
concepts.description: Updating or fitting a model on a local device or environment rather than centralized infrastructure.

concepts.name: Differential privacy
concepts.description: A privacy technique that limits how much information about any individual can be inferred from outputs.

concepts.name: Secure aggregation
concepts.description: A protocol for combining client updates without exposing individual client data to the server.

concepts.name: Privacy budget
concepts.description: A quantitative limit on privacy loss allowed by a differentially private system.

concepts.name: Connectivity constraint
concepts.description: A limitation caused by unreliable, slow, expensive, or unavailable network access.

concepts.name: Device heterogeneity
concepts.description: Variation across devices in hardware, software, sensors, memory, power, and performance.
